free_tier.stated: the `nano` plan starts at just $0.054/hour, billed by the second

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a sandbox, not an object; each file read or write is capped at 100 MiB per call

retention.stated: Stopping keeps /workspace and resets everything else; 'you've got up to 7 days to start() it again before it's permanently deleted'. Only /workspace survives a stop, and failed sandboxes lose /workspace.

egress.terms: Public internet egress is allowed, inbound connections are refused, and no per-GB egress price or allowance is published; both egress and ingress are capped at 200 Mbit/s.

interface_detail: Python SDK ('Sandbox.create(plan="medium")') and an HTTP API, with a dashboard at deepinfra.com/dash/sandboxes.
tooling: The vendor's Python SDK and REST API; commands run inside the microVM and files move only through /workspace.
chaining: USD 0.054 an hour for the nano plan is USD 39.42 a month if never stopped, and a sandbox auto-stops after 24 hours of continuous running, so it is not an always-on machine. It belongs in the stack as a scratch executor next to earlier inference accounts, not as an answer to the cheap-VM questions.

limits.value: auto-stop after 24 continuous running hours, a default 1-hour idle timeout that cannot be disabled, and 7 days of stopped retention before deletion
25 non-stopped sandboxes per account; 'shared-fleet capacity can temporarily prevent creation'

limits_note: Billing runs while a sandbox is creating, starting, running or stopping, so 'per-second' includes boot and the disk save on stop. The plan shapes and rates are behind an authenticated catalog: GET /v1/sandboxes/catalog returned {"detail":"User is not authorized to access this resource"} to an unauthenticated request on 2026-10-24, and the docs say explicitly not to hardcode the numbers.
binding_note: The 24-hour auto-stop is the first hard wall: no configuration on the pages read lifts it, so the machine cannot be an always-on monitor or VPN node even before the price matters.

identity_cost.detail: A DeepInfra account is required and sandboxes draw on DeepInfra billing; the catalog endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller, so plan shapes and prices are visible only to a signed-in account. Card types, any authorisation hold, and whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted were not established.

reliability_note: Two documented loss paths: a failed sandbox loses /workspace, and everything outside /workspace is discarded on stop. Shared-fleet capacity can refuse creation.
confidence_note: The nano rate, the per-second meter and the whole lifecycle are quoted from DeepInfra's own blog and docs, read today. The rate-to-shape mapping is not documented publicly: the vendor directs readers to an authenticated catalog, so the shape fields stay null rather than guessed. What would raise it: a signed-in read of /v1/sandboxes/catalog, which would give the exact vCPU/RAM/disk of the nano plan.

notes: Arithmetic: USD 0.054 an hour × 730 = USD 39.42 a month if the auto-stop did not exist; × 300 h = USD 16.20. The auto-stop makes the 730-hour figure hypothetical, and it is recorded as the price of the meter rather than the price of a machine. What the nano shape actually contains is unverified because the catalog is authenticated. The dossier already carries a DeepInfra record for its DeepStart programme; this is a different product from the same vendor and does not supersede it.
